units: pixels (x right, y down, origin top-left) and seconds

camera.evidence: clean background strips identical between frame 0 and 72 (mean abs diff < 2, noise only); horizon and underwater boundary fixed

layout.sea_surface_band: grey-blue, y ~565-672 (boat sits here; boat reflection y ~645-672)
layout.underwater: uniform bright blue, y 673-1079 (cut-away underwater view; the shark swims here)

objects.name: boat
objects.description: red fishing boat with white cabin, mast and rear railings, hull lettering 'AH805'; bow points left
objects.visible_frames: 0-72 (stern and right part cut by the right image edge in frames 0-25; mast top cut by the top edge in all frames)
objects.motion: translates left, horizontally only; frames 0 and 1 are identical, then about -17.8 px/frame (x) every frame, steady; no vertical motion

extents_px.keel_note: hull meets its reflection at y ~645 (dark contact line at 646-648); y 648-672 is reflection
extents_px.mast: thin pole, about 120 px right of the cabin's left edge, runs off the top of the frame: full height NOT measurable

objects.reference_point: ref_x = bow_x + 428.5 (centre of the full 858-px horizontal extent, valid even while clipped); ref_y = 441 (centre of keel y 645 to cabin roof y 237; constant). True Blender origin unknown, but the boat is rigid and only translates, so displacements and speeds are the same for any point

objects.name: shark
objects.description: grey-and-white shark (dorsal fin, crescent tail) swimming underwater below the boat, facing left
objects.motion: swims left horizontally; frames 0 and 1 identical, then speeds up steadily: per-frame dx about -8 px at the start, rising to about -18 px by frame 72; y constant (centroid y 905.4 +- 0.2)

extents_px.length_range: 266-274 over the clip (fins and tail barely change)
extents_px.note: the snout is rendered semi-transparent. The mask loses about 5-9 px of the nose tip, so the true nose-to-tail length is about 275 px

objects.reference_point: ref = mask bbox centre (bbox_cx, bbox_cy); the mask centroid is also given (it sits about 23 px left of the bbox centre, toward the heavier head)

events.event: both objects stationary (frame 1 identical to frame 0)
motion start, boat and shark (first displacement)
events.note: displacement first seen between frames 1 and 2

events.event: boat stern enters the frame (full boat visible)

events.note: the boat's bow is left of (ahead of) the shark's nose in every frame (frame 0: bow 1496 vs nose ~1530; frame 72: bow 227 vs nose ~632). The gap grows because the boat is faster for most of the clip; no crossing

events.event: end of clip, both still moving left

no_events: no bounces, collisions, contacts or direction changes
